comments.note: project-detail.js line 510: The renderRunsList function is defined as a nested closure inside the getRunLogs().then() callback to close over sorted, repo, slug, and activeFilename. A prior code comment (added before WP-013) already flags this as a 'refactor candidate' — now that repo is also captured, extraction to a module-level helper accepting (sorted, repo, slug, activeFilename, matchingQueueEntry) would improve testability and reduce closure depth. Not fixed here as it's out of scope.

orchestrator-widgets.js renderLogPreview was still using the legacy bare-slug API.getRunLogEntries(slug, filename, afterLine) signature — not covered by any WP in this plan. The orchestrator.js call site (line 420) was already passing the 4-argument form (repo, slug), confirming orchestrator.js was ahead of the widget implementation.

project-detail.js: The reset modal (showResetModal) escapes slug in the modal title heading (escapeHtml(slug)) but could also display the repo for clarity in multi-repo environments. This is a UX enhancement, not a bug — deferred as out of scope.

comments.note: project-detail.js lines 506-508: Stale inline refactor-candidate comment omitted `repo` from the list of closed-over variables and the suggested module-level helper signature. The comment was written when only `(sorted, slug, activeFilename)` were captured; WP-013 added `repo`. Fixed: both occurrences of the signature now read `(sorted, repo, slug, activeFilename, matchingQueueEntry)`. Non-behavioral — comment only.

project-detail.js: renderProjectDetail correctly drains _pdLogPreviewCleanups at the top of every call, preventing interval leaks across SPA navigations. The double-drain pattern (once at top of renderProjectDetail, once at top of renderRunsList) is intentional and correct — the nested drain guards against the kill-button callback re-rendering the runs list without a full page reload.

orchestrator-widgets.js: renderLogPreview cleanup function correctly sets stopped=true before clearInterval, preventing any in-flight fetch from updating the DOM after cleanup. The guard `if (stopped) return` inside fetchEntries is the correct defensive pattern for async polling.

project-detail.js line 181: ProjectNameCache.set(repo + '/' + slug, displayTitle) correctly uses the namespaced key to prevent same-slug collisions across repos, as flagged in the WP-008 code-smell observation. The separator character '/' is safe since slugs are validated to [a-z0-9-]+ and repo names cannot contain '/' in this context.
